lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: finishing the loop

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
objective: Learners pick one real household routine task they have already practiced this unit, such as a space reset or a storage system, complete it once, check the result against a specific standard for what 'done' looks like, identify one specific gap between their result and that standard, then correct the gap and compare their first attempt to their corrected result.
scenario: The learner selects one task they have practiced earlier in this unit, such as resetting a shared space or storing a group of items, and treats finishing as a two-part loop: first completing the task, then checking it against a clear standard and fixing whatever doesn't yet meet it, instead of stopping as soon as the task looks roughly done.
materials: one real household task the learner has already practiced this unit
paper or a notes app to write the standard and the gap

tasks.directions: Pick one task from earlier this unit and write down what 'done' specifically looks like for it before you start.

prompts.text: Name the task you're redoing and write two or three specific things that must be true for it to count as fully done.

tasks.directions: Complete the task once, straight through, without stopping to fix anything along the way.

prompts.text: I completed the whole task in one pass before checking it against my standard.
I did not stop partway through to redo or fix anything.
I wrote down what my finished first attempt actually looked like.

tasks.directions: Check your finished first attempt against the specific standard you wrote in the warm-up and find any gap between them.

prompts.text: Compare your first attempt to your written standard and name one specific thing that doesn't yet match, such as a spot still cluttered, an item not yet stored correctly, or a step skipped.
Fix that specific gap, then describe exactly what you changed to close it.

tasks.directions: Compare your first attempt to your corrected result.

prompts.text: Explain what your first attempt was missing that your standard caught, and why checking your own work against a specific standard is different from just deciding a task 'looks done.'

remediation: If a learner's stated standard is too vague to check against, such as 'make it nice,' reteach by rewriting the standard as two or three yes-or-no checkable statements, for example 'every item has a specific spot' instead of 'organized,' then have the learner re-run the check against the rewritten standard.
extension: Have the learner apply the same finish-and-check loop to a different task from earlier in the unit and compare how large the gap was between their first attempt and their standard on this new task versus the original one.
